metadata.summary: MIMIC-IV is a large, freely available database comprising de-identified health-related data associated with over two hundred thousand patients who were admitted to the critical care units and the hospital of the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston, Massachusetts, USA, between 2008 and 2022. The database includes demographics, vital signs, laboratory tests, medications, observations, and notes.
metadata.purpose: To support a wide range of research including early warning systems, risk prediction, causal inference, and interpretability of clinical machine learning models.

papers.title: MIMIC-IV, a freely accessible electronic health record dataset

modality.scope: Critical care and general hospital admissions

ethics.privacy_measures: De-identification performed per HIPAA Safe Harbor guidelines; protected health information removed or generalized.
ethics.legal_compliance: Complies with HIPAA and institutional IRB requirements.

known_limitations: Single-center origin limits generalizability across institutions, regions, and healthcare systems.
Temporal shifts in clinical practice, coding standards (e.g., ICD-9 to ICD-10), and technology not fully adjusted for.
Underrepresentation of non-English speakers, uninsured, rural, pediatric, and geriatric subpopulations.
Potential selection bias: only patients admitted to a tertiary academic medical center are included.
bias_and_limitations.modifications: Yes — data underwent de-identification and structural transformation (e.g., normalization, time alignment, table linking) from raw EHR systems.
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: 90%+ from single US academic medical center; lacks diversity in geography, payer type, and sociodemographic representation.
bias_and_limitations.long_tail_classes: Yes — rare diagnoses, procedures, and phenotypes are underrepresented.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Results may not generalize beyond similar tertiary academic US hospitals; temporal drift (2008–2022) affects model stability.
bias_and_limitations.subgroup_coverage: No explicit subgroup coverage analysis reported; limited demographic detail provided.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: High rates of missingness in labs, vitals, and notes depending on clinical workflow and acuity.

benchmarks: MIMIC-IV benchmark tasks (e.g., mortality prediction, length-of-stay, readmission)
tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Real-time clinical deployment; direct patient care; commercial product integration without additional validation and regulatory review.

data_origin.selection_rationale: Patients admitted to the critical care units and the hospital of the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.
data_origin.data_shifts_overtime: Data collected between 2008 and 2022; known temporal shifts in clinical practice, coding (e.g., ICD-10 transition), and ICU monitoring technology likely present but not explicitly quantified in source.

population.target_population: Adult patients admitted to critical care units and the hospital of Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.
population.inclusion_criteria: Admission to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center between 2008 and 2022.
population.missing_groups: No explicit reporting of underrepresented groups; single-center US academic medical center limits generalizability to pediatric, geriatric, rural, or non-US populations.

annotation.annotation_method: Clinical data extracted and structured from EHR systems; notes may be raw or preprocessed; labels derived from billing codes (e.g., ICD), orders, and documentation.
annotation.labeling_provenance: Labels derived from clinical documentation, billing codes, and system logs; subject to coding practices and documentation variability.
annotation.label_noise_description: Label noise expected due to inconsistent documentation, coding errors, and evolving clinical definitions (e.g., sepsis criteria).
